claims.text: Integrating in situ high-temperature TGA with synchrotron-based XRD enables simultaneous observation and correlation of oxidation kinetics and phase evolution.
The proposed starting material is an unoxidized high-temperature alloy or ceramic.
The experiment exposes the material to controlled high-temperature oxidizing conditions in an integrated TGA-XRD setup.
High-temperature oxidation can produce significant mass change and phase transformations.
Oxide layers evolve during high-temperature oxidation.
Crystalline phases form or transform as high-temperature oxidation proceeds.
The evolving oxide layers and crystalline phases link TGA mass gain to XRD-observed structural transitions.
TGA records an increase in sample mass as oxidation proceeds.
Synchrotron-based in situ XRD detects phase transitions during oxidation.
Time-correlating TGA and XRD data reveals how oxidation kinetics are directly related to phase stability and transformation.
The integrated method will produce a synchronized dataset in which the onset and rate of mass gain are accompanied by distinct diffraction-pattern changes.
Synchronized TGA and XRD observations can establish a direct relationship between oxidation events and phase evolution.
Independent TGA and ex situ or separately performed in situ XRD do not provide real-time cross-correlated mass and structural data.
Instrument temporal resolution may prevent the method from capturing extremely rapid oxidation.
Subtle phase transformations may be missed when diffraction sensitivity or temporal resolution is insufficient.
The quantitative correlation between mass change and phase transformation may depend on the material system and oxidation rate.
Further calibration may be required before the integrated method can be generalized across materials.
A significant mass change without a corresponding XRD alteration, or a phase change without concurrent mass change, would falsify the proposed direct correlation.
